T: Swap houses. Keep the cheese board.
D: Two heartbroken women swap homes for Christmas, one in Surrey and one in Los Angeles.
P: Serve the snacks when Amanda opens the door of the snowy Surrey cottage.
S: Aged cheddar, brie and blue cheese with oatcakes, quince paste, apple and walnuts
Aged cheddar, brie and blue cheese with oatcakes, quince paste, apple slices and walnuts on a wooden board by the fire.
Amanda lasts one quiet night, then stays. Mustard cheddar toast.

Thick sourdough toast spread with a sauce of vintage cheddar, ale, English mustard and Worcestershire, grilled until bubbling and brown in spots. Melt 20g butter, stir in 1 tbsp plain flour and cook 1 minute, then whisk in 80ml ale. Add 200g grated vintage cheddar, 1 tsp English mustard and a dash of Worcestershire and stir over low heat until thick and smooth. Toast 6 slices of sourdough. Spread the cheese mixture thickly to the edges and grill for 3 to 4 minutes until bubbling and browned in spots. Cut in half and serve hot.
LA pool house green goddess crudités
baby carrots, radishes and snow peas on ice, avocado herb dip, for Amanda who can't cry

Baby carrots, radishes, cucumber and snow peas on ice around a bright green goddess dip of avocado, herbs, lemon and Greek yoghurt. Blitz an avocado, 150g Greek yoghurt, a handful each of parsley, basil and chives, a garlic clove, 2 anchovies, the juice of a lemon and salt until smooth and green. Trim 2 bunches baby carrots and a bunch of radishes, cut a Lebanese cucumber into batons and trim 150g snow peas. Arrange the vegetables over a tray of crushed ice with the dip in the middle.
M: Dinner with Arthur, who tells Iris she is the leading lady

Whole chicken rubbed with lemon and thyme butter, roasted golden, with crisp roast potatoes, honey glazed carrots and gravy made from the pan. Mix 60g soft butter with lemon zest, chopped thyme and salt and push under the skin of a 1.8kg chicken. Put the halved lemon inside. Roast at 200C for 75 minutes. Parboil 1kg potatoes, rough them up and roast in oil alongside for an hour. Glaze 500g carrots with butter and honey. Rest the chicken, then stir flour into the pan juices and whisk in 300ml stock for gravy.
Spaghetti in a slow-simmered tomato and butter sauce with basil and parmesan
Spaghetti with a slow tomato and butter sauce simmered 45 minutes with a halved onion, finished with basil and lots of parmesan, simple enough for the girls to love.
W: Warm date sponge soaked in hot toffee sauce
Date sponge baked at 180C for 35 minutes, poked and soaked with a toffee sauce of brown sugar, butter and cream, served warm with vanilla ice cream.
K: Red wine warmed with orange, cinnamon, cloves, star anise and honey
Red wine warmed slowly with orange, cinnamon, cloves, star anise and honey, never boiled, ladled into mugs.

m.note: Spaghetti in a slow-simmered tomato and butter sauce with basil and parmesan
m.how: Simmer 2 cans crushed tomatoes with 80g butter and a peeled halved onion for 45 minutes, stirring now and then. Remove the onion and season. Toss with 500g cooked spaghetti, then finish with torn basil and plenty of grated parmesan.

w.note: Warm date sponge soaked in hot toffee sauce
w.how: Soak 200g chopped dates in 250ml boiling water with a pinch of bicarb. Cream 60g butter with 150g brown sugar, add 2 eggs, the dates and 175g self-raising flour. Bake at 180C for 35 minutes, poke holes and pour over hot toffee sauce. Serve with ice cream.

d.note: Red wine warmed with orange, cinnamon, cloves, star anise and honey
d.how: Pour a bottle of red wine into a pot with a sliced orange, 2 cinnamon sticks, 4 whole cloves, a star anise and 2 tbsp honey. Warm gently for 20 minutes, never letting it boil. Ladle into mugs by the fire with snow falling outside.
